questions.q: Why does manual, host-by-host hardening break down as a fleet grows?
options: New hosts get provisioned unhardened from a base image, and existing hosts silently drift out of compliance over time through patches, manual edits, and reinstalls
CIS Benchmarks only apply to a single server and cannot be reused on others
Linux servers automatically re-harden themselves after a certain number of days
Manual hardening is actually faster than any automated approach at any scale
questions.explain: At scale, new hosts come up unhardened and existing hosts drift from their original state, and manual, one-at-a-time work can't catch that reliably.

options: A feature that automatically backs up configuration files every night
A type of network latency measured in milliseconds
Hosts silently diverging from their intended hardened state over time, even without anyone deliberately changing a hardening setting
The process of migrating a server from one cloud provider to another
questions.explain: A patch resetting a config to its package default, or a 2 a.m. manual fix that's never reapplied on top of, are both real causes of drift.

questions.q: What does it mean for a hardening shell script to be idempotent?
options: It can only be run exactly one time ever, on one host
Running it twice produces the same end state as running it once, because it checks current state before changing anything
It deletes itself automatically after execution
It requires manual confirmation before every single line executes
questions.explain: An idempotent script doesn't blindly re-append the same change every run — it checks whether the change is already in place first.

questions.q: What does the real-world ansible-lockdown project's UBUNTU22-CIS role do?
options: It only hardens a single host and cannot target more than one machine
It encodes each numbered CIS Benchmark recommendation as its own Ansible task, tagged by level and control number, applicable across an inventory of hosts at once
It replaces the Linux kernel entirely with a hardened fork
It is a GUI application for browsing CIS Benchmark PDFs with no automation capability
questions.explain: ansible-lockdown ships CIS Benchmark controls as tagged Ansible tasks, letting a team run a full profile or a subset across many hosts in parallel.

questions.q: What does running a playbook with --check accomplish, and why does it matter for catching drift?
options: It reports what would change without actually changing anything, letting a team see which hosts have diverged from compliance before deciding to fix them
It permanently deletes the playbook after one run
It forces every host to reboot immediately
It has no effect different from running the playbook normally
questions.explain: Check mode surfaces drift (like a setting silently reset by a patch) as a report, which a team can review before applying the real fix.
